## The claim

P4-28: screen-wide, at least one launched drug is selective for both high-aneuploidy and rhabdomyosarcoma cell lines in PRISM

**Prediction if true.** Over every Launched compound in PRISM Repurposing 24Q2 measurable on at least 3 rhabdomyosarcoma lines and at least 20 lines in each aneuploidy arm, with entry 151's tests unchanged (24Q2 LFC, one-sided Mann-Whitney U, strict median aneuploidy split), at least one drug has Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.10 in the aneuploidy contrast and q < 0.10 in the rhabdomyosarcoma contrast, BH taken across all eligible Launched compounds in each contrast

**What would refute it.** No eligible Launched compound reaches q < 0.10 in both contrasts

| 216 | refutes | 0.80 | measurement | Over 613 eligible Launched drugs in PRISM 24Q2, with Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast, no drug reaches q < 0.10 in the rhabdomyosarcoma contrast (best 0.122) or the aneuploidy contrast (best 0.287), so none reaches it in both. | `docs/iteration4/step-10/methodology/154-screen-wide-prism-sweep.md` |
| 217 | neutral | 0.40 | measurement | The same sweep code, run over skin/melanoma lines against the rest, puts dabrafenib and vemurafenib at ranks 1 and 2 of 2,032 Launched drugs (q 3.2e-9 and 4.5e-8), so the null is not a pipeline failure. | `docs/iteration4/step-10/methodology/154-screen-wide-prism-sweep.md` |
| 218 | neutral | 0.30 | measurement | The rhabdomyosarcoma contrast rests on three lines (TE617T, RD, RH30) for 619 of 633 compound copies and fires at 9.6 % raw p < 0.05, twice the nominal rate, so its arm of the test has little power. | `docs/iteration4/step-10/methodology/154-screen-wide-prism-sweep.md` |
